about: evidence_ledger.csv. build refuses entries that break analysis/prelaunch.check_claim (MEASURED needs a source and date; UNTESTED/UNAVAILABLE can't be HIGH; every claim states its limitation).

claims.claim: The 2026-10-25 run's 'outlier' label mostly tracks video age: 3 of 46 English long videos up to 30 days old were outliers vs 59 of 59 older ones.
claims.limitations: Search-discovered videos only; flat-listing dates are approximate.
claims.decision_relevance: The old 'proven niches' cannot be used as evidence of opportunity.

claims.claim: The old dataset counted 15 videos twice (English and Spanish buckets) and scored 11 rows from an unrelated K-pop artist.
claims.limitations: Off-topic detection is a keyword rule; other off-topic rows may remain.
claims.decision_relevance: Old counts (343 scored, 213 on-topic) are inflated.

claims.claim: Inside the same channel, a video's direction label (sleep/zen, meditation, lo-fi, epic) does not change its performance: median 1.00-1.03x the channel's own median for every direction.
claims.source: normalized/all_videos.csv (relative_to_channel, uploads 14-365 days, channels with a usable baseline)
claims.limitations: Keyword-based labels; views above 1,000 rounded to 2-3 significant figures; channels found through search.
claims.decision_relevance: Direction is a channel-level positioning choice; no label buys extra views by itself.

claims.claim: Every direction is crowded: this month's search-visible Japanese-themed uploads number 251-355 per direction from 113-200 channels, with median views of 103-334.
claims.source: raw/validation/fresh_month.json (YouTube search, upload date = this month, 4 queries x 100 per direction)
claims.limitations: A lower bound (100 results per query); views are snapshots of 0-30-day-old uploads.
claims.decision_relevance: No 'empty niche' exists; a beginner competes on quality and distinctiveness.

claims.claim: Search incumbents are strongest in lo-fi (top-60 median 718K views, 44% over 1M) and weakest in epic (36K, 17%).
claims.source: raw/validation/searches.json (relevance order; the date-sort parameter was ignored by YouTube)
claims.limitations: Logged-out search from one location; personalised results differ.
claims.decision_relevance: Search-led discovery is hardest for lo-fi.

claims.claim: Channels under 10K subscribers: typical (median) views of uploads 30-365 days old are ~1,900 for epic (n=200 uploads), ~1,200 for meditation-titled ambient (n=56), ~790 for zen/sleep (n=101) and ~100 for lo-fi (n=10).
claims.limitations: Few channels per cell; lo-fi cell is 10 uploads; channels found through search (survivors); bootstrap intervals overlap.
claims.decision_relevance: No direction is clearly better for a beginner; differences between channels exceed differences between directions.

claims.claim: Channels under a year old that reached thousands of subscribers in the sample are all calm Japanese ambient/meditation channels (Seiiki 15.8K, Zen Drift 3.3K, Ronin Zen Ambience 3.4K, Ronin Soul 1.2K); failures exist in the same directions (Way of Stillness 8 subs, Zen peaceful music 12, Japanese Zen Legends 50).
claims.limitations: Survivorship: channels enter through search; channel age from approximate dates.
claims.decision_relevance: The calm ambient/meditation lane has observed beginner breakouts; lo-fi and epic beginners in the sample stayed under 2K typical views.

claims.claim: Hits are rare and unpredictable within channels: the median channel has 19-28% of its uploads at 2x or more of its own median.
claims.limitations: Rounded view counts; 14-365-day window.
claims.decision_relevance: A pilot needs several independent uploads before judging; one video says little.

claims.claim: Lifetime views/day overstates current velocity: for videos 91-365 days old with 5K+ views, recent daily views were a median 0.49x their lifetime average; over 1 year old, 0.42x.
claims.limitations: One short window including a weekend; 70 videos.
claims.decision_relevance: Benchmarks must use views at matched age, not lifetime averages.

claims.claim: Genuine guided or breathing sessions are essentially absent from Japanese-themed music supply (3 regex hits in ~9,000 listed uploads, all false positives).
claims.limitations: Title keywords only; guided content may exist outside the sampled channels.
claims.decision_relevance: Demand for a samurai breathing product is UNTESTED - no supply to learn from.

claims.claim: Demand for a guided/breathing samurai product exists.
claims.source: autocomplete shows generic 'guided meditation' / 'breathing meditation' intents, not Japanese-themed ones
claims.limitations: Autocomplete shows that queries exist, not their volume.
claims.decision_relevance: Postpone direction C as a breathing product.

claims.claim: No public source gives a verifiable YouTube RPM for lo-fi, zen, sleep or meditation channels.
claims.limitations: Reddit and video income reveals could not be checked.
claims.decision_relevance: Revenue scenarios use illustrative RPMs only; a zero-revenue outcome is possible.

claims.claim: Competitors' retention, CTR, returning viewers and revenue are private.
claims.source: YouTube Studio is private to each channel
claims.limitations: Only public counts are used as proxies.
claims.decision_relevance: Listening-quality claims must come from the owner's own pilot.

claims.claim: ElevenLabs Creator permits online commercial use (incl. monetized YouTube) and streaming distribution; 62 generation / 250 download minutes per month; output may not be unique; no IP warranty on self-serve plans; music-library offers are prohibited.
claims.limitations: Contract terms change; Content ID registration not addressed.
claims.decision_relevance: Music is usable on YouTube once the plan at generation is documented; no downloads or streamer libraries.

claims.claim: The 12 tracks were downloaded on a paid ElevenLabs plan.
claims.source: Music Terms Exhibit A: Free plan downloads 'Not permitted'; the files exist
claims.limitations: No invoice or generation history seen; a plan change between generation and download is possible.
claims.decision_relevance: Likely cleared for YouTube, but NEEDS EVIDENCE until the history page is saved.

claims.claim: Kling members' commercial use of output 'is not restricted' during the membership; whether that survives cancellation is not stated.
claims.limitations: Post-cancellation rights need written clarification.
claims.decision_relevance: Keep Kling until clarified, or rely only on clips whose rights are confirmed in writing.

claims.claim: OpenAI assigns its rights (if any) in image output to the user; commercial use is not restricted; output may not be unique; no real-person likeness without consent.
claims.limitations: Prompts and original files not recorded.
claims.decision_relevance: Images usable; keep the character fictional, not Yasuke.

claims.claim: Purely AI-generated material is not protected by US copyright; prompts and selecting an output are not authorship; minor technical edits such as EQ are unlikely to qualify.
claims.source: US Copyright Office, Copyright and AI Part 2 (Jan 2025), pp. iii, 18-24
claims.limitations: US law; the EQ point is an inference from the report, which does not mention EQ; Dominican Ley 65-00 not checked.
claims.decision_relevance: The owner holds contractual permission, not exclusive rights; Content ID and dispute positions are weak.

claims.claim: Content ID requires exclusive rights and excludes non-exclusive licences, soundbeds/loops and continuous DJ mixes.
claims.limitations: Neither page mentions AI music.
claims.decision_relevance: Do not plan on Content ID income or protection.

claims.claim: YouTube requires the altered/synthetic disclosure when AI 'creates music that's the main focus of the video'; disclosure alone doesn't limit reach or monetization.
claims.limitations: Undated help page.
claims.decision_relevance: Disclose on every video.

claims.claim: YPP entry for new creators rises to 8,000 watch hours (or 20M Shorts views) plus 1,000 subscribers from 2027-02-01.
claims.limitations: Policy may change again.
claims.decision_relevance: A channel launched now will almost surely face the 8,000-hour bar.

claims.claim: Monetization does not apply to content that 'looks like it's made with a template' or AI content giving 'the impression of mass production'; reviewers look at the channel as a whole.
claims.limitations: No rule for ambient/static-loop music; judged case by case.
claims.decision_relevance: Distinct music and visual variation per video are a monetization requirement, not a nicety.

claims.claim: The quote set presents 9 modern authors' lines and 3 well-known misattributions as samurai wisdom; only 4 lines trace to samurai texts (as paraphrases) and 1 is a proverb.
claims.source: quote provenance check of INPUT/TEXT/samurai_wisdom.json (web sources per quote in rights_matrix.csv)
claims.limitations: Generic lines were not all searched; several attributions are LOW confidence.
claims.decision_relevance: The two quote renders are BLOCKED until the set is corrected.

claims.claim: The tracks were loudness-normalised and peak-limited, not only EQ'd: true peaks moved from about 0 dBTP (one at +0.2) to -1.3/-1.5 dBTP, integrated loudness to -13.5/-14.3 LUFS, and loudness range shrank (e.g. 9.5 to 4.5 LU).
claims.source: raw/audio_audit.json (ebur128 on originals vs published files)
claims.limitations: The 'originals' carry an ffmpeg encoder tag and may themselves be re-encoded.
claims.decision_relevance: Consistent levels are good; the dynamics loss matters for meditative listening.

claims.claim: The 12-track set mixes two promises: 6 tracks have a clear steady beat (clarity >= 0.5) and the rest are freer or soft-pulse pieces.
claims.limitations: Automatic beat measure; needs a listening check.
claims.decision_relevance: Split beat tracks and calm tracks into different videos.

claims.claim: Two same-prompt tracks (Samurai Morning Drift, Samurai Stillness) share a passage clearly above the unrelated-pair baseline; four tracks form a group of mutually similar passages.
claims.limitations: An engineering signal for a listening check - not proof of duplication or of legal originality.
claims.decision_relevance: Listen to those pairs; don't place them back to back.

claims.claim: Every track fades out at its end and most start at full level within half a second, so the 43:39 video has abrupt restarts after near-silence at most joins.
claims.limitations: RMS levels; perceived abruptness needs a listening check.
claims.decision_relevance: Add short fade-ins or crossfades for calm listening.

claims.claim: The finished video loops one 6-second Kling clip ~379 times (plus 26 slow-motion pauses) and shows a new quote every 11.15 s (234 showings); render of the light+scroll version took 86.8 minutes.
claims.limitations: Render time on this computer only.
claims.decision_relevance: Visual repetition and constant text are the variables the viewer test must check.

claims.claim: The rendered video has no flashing risk: no frame-to-frame luminance change of 10% or more over a 2-minute sample; the speaker light varies within a small luminance band.
claims.limitations: One 2-minute window.
claims.decision_relevance: Light effects are safe; their value is a taste question for the viewer test.

claims.claim: A visible character, speaker light, equalizer or quote scroll improves listening or retention.
claims.source: none of the 7 winning openings reviewed uses a visualizer or breathing guide; 3 of 7 open with a quote card
claims.limitations: No retention data is public.
claims.decision_relevance: Test offline (V1/V2/V3) before publishing, then with Test & Compare.

claims.claim: 'Black samurai' has no observed listening demand: 'black samurai lofi' returns no suggestions of its own; 'yasuke' completes to the game, film and controversy.
claims.limitations: Autocomplete is not volume.
claims.decision_relevance: Use the character as a visual identity, not as a search keyword.

claims.claim: YouTube Partner Program and AdSense payment (check, wire, Hyperwallet) are available in the Dominican Republic; with no US-DR tax treaty, 30% is withheld from US-viewer earnings.
claims.limitations: Dominican income-tax treatment (Ley 11-92 Art. 269/272) needs a local accountant.
claims.decision_relevance: The simplest setup is an individual account with W-8BEN; no US company needed.

claims.claim: Whether YouTube income is Dominican-source (taxable) or foreign-source for a DR resident individual.
claims.limitations: Needs professional advice.
claims.decision_relevance: Ask an accountant before income starts; irrelevant while revenue is zero.

claims.claim: With ElevenLabs Creator (62 generation minutes a month) the owner can make about one 45-minute video of unique music per month.
claims.source: economics.json scenarios; Music Terms Exhibit A
claims.limitations: Kept share is an assumption (0.4-0.9); variants per generation and their minute cost unknown.
claims.decision_relevance: A 4-6-video pilot on Creator takes 4-6 months; Pro (304 minutes) fits it in about one month.

claims.claim: Sleep listeners resist ads ('japanese music for sleep no ads', 'samurai sleep music no ads'), and YouTube says meditation videos may not suit mid-rolls.
claims.limitations: Autocomplete is not volume.
claims.decision_relevance: Ad income per hour of sleep/meditation listening is likely lower; prefer calm focus as the promise.

claims.claim: Viewers comment mostly about peace and healing; explicit requests (track names, permission to use music on streams, 'is it AI?') are rare.
claims.source: comments.json of 9 videos (294 comments) in the 2026-10-25 evidence
claims.limitations: Self-selected commenters; 9 videos; keyword themes.
claims.decision_relevance: Weak signal only; real listening needs come from the pilot and the blind test.
